title: Using a plot fragment with generalized constraints
known_facts_from_text: DAVID is married; his wife's father ALEX is nasty enough (niceness < 0) to threaten DAVID (L85-TR p. 21).
RENEE does not have a nasty father-in-law, so the original forced-marriage does not apply.

lines.raw: -- using plan FORCED-MARRIAGE0 {FORCED-MARRIAGE with generalized constraints}
working on goal -- (DO-THREATEN ALEX DAVID "forget it") -- using plan THREATEN
>>> DAVID tells RENEE he doesn't love her
working on goal -- (WORRY-ABOUT RENEE) -- using plan BE-CONCERNED
Possible candidates -- MARLENA JULIE DOUG ROMAN DON CHRIS KAYLA
Several plans to choose from ATTEMPTED-MURDER EXPOSE

observations: Role mapping after generalisation: ?her=DAVID (the married one), ?him=RENEE. The paper notes role names 'are now rather misleading'.

(TOGETHER * RENEE) is satisfied by 'RENEE seduces ROMAN', the churned lover is the seducer, unlike Figs. 4–5. Suggests SEDUCTION binds the wildcard role to the seduced party or that '*' can bind either role. UNRESOLVED (Q-PF-3).
Trace ends after ELIMINATE (no divorce, no final disjunction shown). Figure presumably truncated.
published_version: Poetics 14 (1985) Table 10, p. 500: the same lines, with the DUMP-LOVER and SEDUCTION plan names on the goal line, and a final line "..." after ">>> STEPHANO tries to kill ALEX": the published figure marks the trace as cut, not finished.
